companyIntro.name: Terra Spatial
companyIntro.mission: Turn location data into decisions for infrastructure and cities.
companyIntro.culture: Coordinate systems are never assumed. Data lineage and accuracy are documented.

projectBackground.name: Flood Risk Atlas — Riverside District
projectBackground.context: The municipality needs to know which parcels are within a flood buffer and how reliable the data is.

manager.name: Femke de Boer
manager.role: Head of Spatial Analysis, Terra Spatial
manager.note: Never assume a coordinate system. A map that looks right can still measure wrong.

assignment.title: Build the flood buffer analysis
assignment.brief: Convert map scale, compute buffer area, calculate parcel areas in Excel, address projection issues and explain a spatial join.

documents.name: Map Sheet
documents.note: Map scale 1:5,000; a feature measures 4 cm on the map.

documents.name: Buffer Request
documents.note: 100 m flood buffer around a pump station.

documents.name: Layer Metadata
documents.note: Parcels in one coordinate system, flood data in another.

tasks.title: Map Scale
tasks.prompt: On a 1:5,000 map a feature is 4 cm long. What is the real length (m)?
tasks.reasoning: Scale converts map to ground distance.
tasks.mistake: Forgetting cm to m conversion gives 20,000 m.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Buffer Area
tasks.prompt: A 100 m radius buffer. What is the area in m² (round to nearest unit)?
tasks.mistake: Buffering in degrees gives meaningless results.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Coordinate Systems
tasks.prompt: Parcels and flood data use different coordinate systems. What should you do before analysis?
options: Reproject both to a common projected CRS suitable for measurement
tasks.reasoning: Mismatched CRS misaligns layers and distorts measurements.
tasks.tip: Check the CRS of every layer.
tasks.mistake: Overlaying without reprojection gives offsets of hundreds of metres.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Spatial Join
tasks.prompt: What does a spatial join do?
options: Transfers attributes between layers based on location
tasks.reasoning: Location, not a key, links the records.
tasks.mistake: Confusing it with an attribute join gives wrong results.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Parcel Areas (Excel)
tasks.prompt: Area in m² (D = B x C) and in hectares (E = D / 10000). Upload for checking.
tasks.mistake: Mixing m² and ha is a common error.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Planner Explanation
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence explanation of how you identified parcels in the flood buffer.
tasks.modelAnswer: I reprojected the parcel and flood layers to a single metric coordinate system, created a 100 m buffer around the pump station (about 3.14 hectares) and ran a spatial join to flag parcels that intersect it. Data accuracy is limited by the source scale, so parcels near the edge should be verified on site. I documented the sources, projection and date so the analysis can be repeated.
tasks.reasoning: A good explanation covers method, limits and reproducibility.
tasks.mistake: Maps without lineage can't be defended.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Shifted Map
caseStudy.background: A city overlaid parcels and flood zones in different coordinate systems. Layers were offset by 140 m and 60 homes were wrongly told they were safe.
caseStudy.constraints: The mismatch wasn't visible at city scale.
questions: What check would have caught it?
caseStudy.solution: Terra introduced mandatory CRS checks and a metadata sign-off before any analysis.
